judgements.justification: B's meta-review states no reading of its own that goes past the reviews ('a solid work worthy of acceptance' argues only for acceptance); the spotlight is a bare tier call, which R18 covers, not an area chair's own taste.
Neither area chair nor any reviewer forecast impact beyond the paper's setting; both accepted the limited real-world relevance.
The rebuttal lifted A's Reviewer_Pvqb from 6 to 7, which brought A into line with B's 7s; it narrowed the gap and did not cause the split.

B's spotlight rests on about 9 hours over three reviews, including Reviewer_Gr4i (2 h, 'not familiar with the key related works', misread rho) and Reviewer_1153's generic praise, against about 20 hours and the only substantive questions in A.
Only A raised the Algorithm 1, PAC-label and novelty questions, but the rebuttal settled them and none counted against the paper in A's poster or meta-review.
Reviewers on both committees weighed the same strengths and limits the same way and all rated 7; the split lies in the tier mapping, not in weight given to a shared strength or weakness.
No score moved through reviewer discussion; B's Reviewer_Gr4i read the other reviews and kept 7.
Every reviewer's 7 matches a positive text with minor remarks; no rating contradicts its own review.
Unsure reviewers sat on both committees (B's Gr4i, A's Sk3C at confidence 2), and all rated 7, an accept score, not a borderline one.
No reviewer stood apart on either committee; all seven final ratings are 7.
The two committees placed similar verdicts at the same score, 7, so no calibration gap exists.
A was equally unanimous (four 7s) and got a poster, and B's meta-review does not cite agreement as grounds for the tier, so unanimity does not explain the split.
No score rose on unverified rebuttal evidence; Pvqb's rise rested on a correct explanation of Algorithm 1 that the camera-ready keeps.
A's meta-review omits the settled caveats yet A got the lower tier, and B's meta-review carries the real-world limitation forward, so no one-sided summary lifted either committee.
Pvqb's misreading of Algorithm 1 was corrected before his final 7, and Gr4i's misreading of rho did not bear on his 7, so no wrong claim fed a final score or tier.
The authors conceded nothing damaging beyond the shared, already-stated lack of practical relevance.
No objection or score cut came after the author-response period on either committee.

Both committees rated the paper 7 throughout (four 7s in A, three in B) with no reviewer arguing for a highlight, and neither meta-review gives a reason for its tier; A's area chair chose poster and B's chose spotlight on the same profile.
No best-informed reviewer reached a verdict that differed from the rest; A's most thorough reviewer, Pvqb, also ended at 7.
A's concerns were answerable and the rebuttal answered them, but B had no concerns to answer, and the answer only brought A up to B's scores.
No outlying score exists; all final ratings are 7.
No reviewer's score stood apart from their committee.

reasoning: Stage 1 finds the spotlight/poster split an area chair tier call on identical reviews: all seven reviewers rated 7, none argued for a highlight, and neither meta-review explains its tier. That is R18 as defined. The only other difference is scrutiny: B's spotlight rests on three short reviews, two thin, while A's four reviews held every substantive question, all settled in the rebuttal, so R04 applies. The A-only concerns, the rebuttal rise and the misreadings either were resolved or narrowed the gap, so R03, R05 and R15 do not apply. The stage 1 candidates (AC discretion, meta-reviews silent on tier, no reviewer arguing for a highlight, thin spotlight-side reviews, doubts settled only in A) map onto R18 and R04, so no reason is added.
